farmhand.name: Farmhand
farmhand._sheetsNote: The blighted repaint, and it is a readability fix rather than a dressing change. The delivered farmhand wore the player's straw hat and blue dungarees at the player's own size, so at wave 6 -- with the density pass putting 2.2x as many of them on the field -- you could not pick yourself out of the crowd. `farmhandBlight` is that same rig repainted offline by `npm run recolour`: rotted-black hat, rot-green cloth, pale sick-green skin. Stated here rather than in art/sprites.json because WHICH SHEET AN ENEMY WEARS is content, and `world.spawnEnemy` already reads this field.
farmhand.teaches: chaff that makes AoE feel good

crow.name: Carrion Crow
crow._note: Generated in an earlier session for the Crow Bell and left unpacked -- eight rotations, a hop, a recoil and a death, all bought. Wired in session 25 rather than left as art nothing drew. It FLANKS like the feral dog but without the bark: small groups, fragile, fast, arriving from the side you are not watching while the herd holds your eye in front.
crow._weightNote: ZERO, and this is the mechanism that actually holds an enemy out. The spawner reads `map.enemyBias[id] ?? def.weight ?? 1`, so an enemy with no bias entry and no weight defaults to ONE and spawns on EVERY map. Deleting the crow's two bias entries did not remove it from the game, it promoted it from 0.9 on the Bone Orchard to 1.0 everywhere -- and the next test run failed on a different bot for a reason that looked unrelated. The comment above that line in spawner.ts already said how this is done: sit at weight 0 until a map raises you. A map entry REPLACES this rather than multiplying it, so putting `"crow": 0.9` in a map's enemyBias is all it takes to switch on.
crow._costNote: 4 and not 3. At cost 3 with xp 2 the crow was the most XP-EFFICIENT body in the roster -- 0.67 xp per point of threat against 0.5 for the rooster and hen and 0.4 for the feral dog -- and the wave budget is FIXED, so it did not add bodies, it made the same budget pay out more. tests/run.test.ts caught it on the first run: the Hand idle-buy bot cleared 7 of 24 standing still against a cap of 5. Session 24 had already written down why, in words -- arrivals are xp -- and this is that sentence with a number on it. At cost 4 it pays 0.5, in line with the other birds.
crow._rotationNote: BUILT AND NOT IN ROTATION, deliberately. No map gives the crow a weight, so it never spawns; enabling it is one line per map (`"crow": 0.9` in boneOrchard's enemyBias, 0.6 in theBurn's). It is held out because it FAILS the idle-buy bar in tests/run.test.ts and that bar is the owner's to move, not a passing session's. Measured, 24 seeds, The Hand standing still: at threatCost 3 it cleared 7/24, at threatCost 4 it cleared 6/24, against a cap of 5. The wave budget is fixed, so a new enemy type does not add bodies -- it redistributes them -- and any crow priced to be worth fighting is also worth xp. Session 24 said it in words: arrivals are xp. Raising the cap to fit was not considered; a guard relaxed until it passes is worse than no guard.
crow.teaches: they come from behind, in threes

special._note: Growth was 30/s over 6s, which is a final radius of 270 — a cloud wider than the 520px camera view. That was survivable while the cloud was decoration; once it damaged the player it was not a hazard you could play around, it was a tax with no visible edge. 10/s lands at 150, which fills half the screen and can still be walked out of.

maskedHauler.teaches: read the field, not the nearest target

_lateRosterNote: The five below all existed as complete 8-direction rigs in the atlas -- walk, attack, death and idle, 224 frames each -- and were wired to nothing. 1,120 frames, 26% of the packed atlas, already paid for and never drawn. They are placed at waves 3, 8, 13, 16 and 19 rather than spread evenly, because the roster's real gap was the back half: before this, the last new enemy arrived at wave 14 and waves 15-25 introduced nothing at all. Nearly half a run was the same eight things getting bigger numbers.

infectedHen.name: Infected Hen
infectedHen.teaches: a cloud you cannot aim through

fjordPonyCursed.name: Cursed Fjord Pony
fjordPonyCursed.teaches: the first thing that is both quick and solid

arabianCursed.name: Cursed Arabian
arabianCursed._note: The Hog's charge, read faster: shorter wind-up, higher top speed, longer overshoot and a briefer stagger. The Hog teaches you that a charge has a reward window; this one teaches you the window is not always the same size.
arabianCursed.teaches: the same tell, on a shorter fuse

donkeyCursed.name: Cursed Donkey
donkeyCursed._note:
flank is the Feral Dog's behaviour and nothing else has used it since wave 4. On a 30hp dog getting behind you is a nuisance; at 165hp it is the reason to keep moving. Same code, twelve waves later, a different problem.

It was knockbackImmune for one pass and that was a mistake, caught by measurement rather than by eye: a flanker that cannot be pushed off is aimed squarely at the one class whose kit is standing still. The crossover test measured The Hand's preference for holding ground at 21-vs-11 without these enemies and 26-vs-21 with them -- the gap halved, and this card was why. Knockback restored; it still gets behind you, you can still shove it.
donkeyCursed.teaches: check behind you, again, when it matters

draftMuleCursed.name: Cursed Draft Mule
draftMuleCursed._note: The heaviest thing in the game short of a boss, and the only new enemy after wave 16. First pass was 360hp with knockback immunity AND 45% frontal reduction -- three defensive layers at once, where maskedHauler at 220hp has none of them. Six seeds went to one. Frontal reduction dropped and the numbers pulled back; knockback immunity stays, because being unable to stop it is the whole idea and it is the one layer that changes how you play rather than how long you shoot.
draftMuleCursed.teaches: some things are not a fight

phases.desc: Fixed agricultural back-and-forth, laying a gas strip behind it.

bossCockerel.name: The Cockerel
bossCockerel._note: The fast boss. Every boss the roster had was heavy and slow -- the bull charges in a straight line, the duster does not chase at all -- so the shape missing was something light that closes distance and keeps closing. Suggested around wave 9, before the bull.
bossCockerel._rotationNote: BUILT AND NOT IN ROTATION. `weight: 0` keeps it out of the ordinary spawn pool -- the spawner reads `map.enemyBias[id] ?? def.weight ?? 1`, so an enemy with neither defaults to ONE and spawns on every map. A boss additionally only appears if `waves.json` -> `bossWaves` names it against a wave, so switching this on is ONE line there. Held out because a boss changes the shape of a run and that is the owner's call; the art, the stats and the wiring are done and tested.
bossCockerel.teaches: something that is faster than you are

prizeBull.name: The Prize Bull
prizeBull._note: Wave 12 boss (§9). Nine hundred pounds of blue ribbon. Charges in a straight line and hits his own trash on the way through, so a bad build survives long enough to learn what is wrong with it.
prizeBull.teaches: a straight line you can step out of

duster.name: The Duster
duster._note: Wave 25 boss (§9). Nobody is driving it. Phase 1 is a fixed agricultural back-and-forth that NEVER chases — the whole fight is where you stand relative to a machine that will not deviate. Phase 2 breaks the pattern and comes for you while the rows burn inward.
duster._drawScaleNote: Drawn at 2x since v2 critic round 2: at 1x the final boss read smaller than the Prize Bull (97px at 2x) and much like the farm's own tractor. Render only; the hitbox is `radius`.

special._note: Phase 2 starts below phase2BelowPct. gasEvery is how often it drops a strip; the strip is a real gas hazard and hurts you exactly like a Bloated Farmhand cloud.

duster.teaches: a machine that will not deviate

_baseCastNote:
THE BASE CAST SITS AT `weight: 0` AND SPAWNS NOWHERE UNTIL A MAP ASKS FOR IT BY NAME. That is the same mechanism biome node variants use in nodes.json, and it is why adding five enemies to this file changes not one surface wave and not one recorded seed. A map's `enemyBias` entry REPLACES the weight rather than multiplying it, so a base map can raise a zero.
THE NUMBERS BELOW ARE A FIRST PASS AND WANT A PLAY SESSION. They are interpolated from the existing enemies either side of each first-wave -- a guard sits between blownSheep and sickHog, a breacher above maskedHauler -- which is a defensible starting point and is not the same thing as tuned. Balance in this project is a joint activity; nothing here has been measured against a human playing it.

_densityNote: Every spawnable had hp x0.55, damage x0.55 and threatCost x0.45 applied together, which is the change the note on threatBudget in formulas.ts asked for and refused to make by itself: 'more enemies that are individually weaker'. Cutting cost further than hp and damage is what makes it more BODIES rather than the same fight re-priced -- the budget now buys about 2.2x the headcount at 55% of the strength each, so the total hp pool and the total damage potential of a wave barely move while the field actually fills. Bosses (threatCost 0) are untouched. Do not scale one of these three without the other two; that was measured and it just moves difficulty.
